body.cap: AVING News conducted an interview with Dongho Kim, CEO of Safeway, at the AVING Media Stage set up inside the Seoul Pavilion at Eureka Park, Venetian Expo, CES 2026. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Safeway Inc. (CEO Dongho Kim) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), and took part in an interview at the AVING Media Stage inside the Seoul Pavilion during the exhibition period.

Safeway is a startup that has been building AI-based robot platform development capabilities in response to the emerging era of so-called “Mobility of Things (MoT).” By converging autonomous-driving and robotic platform technologies, the company aims to deliver solutions applicable across a wide range of mobility applications and establish itself as a provider of new mobility standards.

In line with this vision, Safeway has developed a solution based on an AI-driven adaptive elastic wheel structure. The technology supports high-speed driving on flat surfaces and provides specialized functions for overcoming obstacles. Its versatility across outdoor autonomous robots, electric wheelchairs, and various forms of personal mobility was recognized with a CES 2026 Innovation Award.

Safeway’s award-winning platform, “Ascender,” is a next-generation personal mobility solution designed to freely overcome stairs and obstacles. By flexibly transforming the wheel shape in response to road conditions and height differences, Ascender can climb obstacles up to 130% of the wheel radius without relying on complex tracks or multi-wheel mechanisms.

In addition, the Ascender platform features a modular design that allows for easy expansion and application. It supports a payload of up to 100 kilograms and speeds of up to 21 kilometers per hour, offering durability and structural rigidity. When applied to personal mobility devices, the platform enables stable driving performance not only in urban environments but also across outdoor off-road terrain, according to the company.

Safeway is currently working with partners, including the Korea Expressway Corporation, Japanese electric wheelchair and mobility brand WHILL, and Stanford University in the United States, to broaden the range of Ascender applications. Building on its participation at CES 2026, the company plans to actively pursue commercialization and expand partnerships both domestically and overseas.

Dongho Kim, CEO of Safeway, said, “Through Ascender, we aim to overcome the mobility limitations of existing robots, unmanned mobility systems, and personal mobility devices,” adding, “We are particularly focusing on the U.S. and Japanese markets, seeking collaboration with local mobility companies to accelerate our global expansion.”

The company participated in CES 2026, held from January 6 to 9, as part of the Seoul Pavilion located in Eureka Park, the startup-focused exhibition area. The Seoul Pavilion at CES 2026 supported a total of 70 startups with participation from 19 startup support organizations based in Seoul, including the Seoul Business Agency, district offices, related institutions, and universities. The 70 exhibiting companies were composed of startups offering products and services based on advanced technologies such as AI, mobility, and healthcare. Among them, selected outstanding companies were given the opportunity to participate in CES’s official media event, Unveiled.
